state:
**Goal `path-literals-follow-up`: Stages 1 to 5 are on disk, and Stage 6's compiler and editor halves are on disk.** Stage 1's floor is goal `plain-comments`'s list.

ADR 0250 states the rule in `rule:types/class-reference`. A plain string literal under `as class<T>` is the class's whole name, `nvs_hir::requires`' harvest loads it through `autoload`, and `nvs-types` reports `E0303` or `E0708` for it.

Completion inside that literal offers every class and interface that is a `T`, loaded or loadable. `nvs_hir::AutoloadMap::loadable_links` (`crates/nvs-hir/src/autoload.rs`) parses each file `enumerate` lists that the program has not loaded, and `HierarchyResolver::written` reads its links. `class_names` checks them against a copy of the graph widened with those links. The analysis now keeps the whole map as `Analysed::autoload`. Every Stage 6 check named in the goal record now has its test on disk.

`rule:ide/completion-offers-only-what-the-compiler-derived` still says the `as class<T>` literal completes as "the classes the program declares". That reads true for a class on an `autoload` root, so the fragment was not edited. The goal has no ADR slot left to amend it.

Stage 4's example 01 (`docs/examples/core/Path/fromCwd/01-a-file-name-from-the-command-line.nvs`) is still only half done: it does not read the file, because the example runner gives no `fs.read` grant at the repository root.

`bun nv proofs --id` reads the roster from a stale `nvs` unless you pass `--nvs` (playbook, Tooling).

An example that converts a literal naming an autoloaded class fits the new behaviour, at `crates/nvs-types/src/expr/operators.rs:127`. Run `bun nv proofs --comments` over every new `.nvs`.
